a. 附带的, 易于发生的, 外来的, 入射的
vocabulary.en:
n. a single distinct event
n. a public disturbance
a. falling or striking of light rays on something
vocabulary.example: She only recognised the incident as discrimination much later.

vocabulary.zh: n. 敌意, 敌对, 反对
vocabulary.en:
n. a hostile (very unfriendly) disposition
n. a state of deep-seated ill-will
n. the feeling of a hostile person
vocabulary.example: She also felt that this kind of public hostility had become less common.

vocabulary.zh:
a. 明显的, 公然的, 蓄意的
[法] 明显的, 公开的
vocabulary.en: a. open and observable; not secret or hidden
vocabulary.example: In both Wales and Finland, older generations remembered more overt hostility.

vocabulary.zh:
n. 其时, 其间
adv. 同时, 于此时
vocabulary.en:
r. at the same time but in another place
r. during the intervening time
vocabulary.example: Younger people, meanwhile, appeared to be growing up with greater acceptance of the minority language.

vocabulary.zh: 少数族群语言
vocabulary.en: a language used by a smaller group within a wider population
vocabulary.example: Younger people, meanwhile, appeared to be growing up with greater acceptance of the minority language.

vocabulary.zh:
n. 可见性, 能见度, 能见距离
[计] 可见性
vocabulary.en:
n. quality or fact or degree of being visible; perceptible by the eye or obvious to the eye
n. degree of exposure to public notice
n. capability of providing a clear unobstructed view
vocabulary.example: This suggests that official recognition and greater visibility can change the status of a language without necessarily eliminating the social attitudes that surround it.

vocabulary.zh:
n. 状态, 情形, 地位, 要人身份
[计] 状态
vocabulary.en: n. the relative position or standing of things or especially persons in a society
vocabulary.example: This suggests that official recognition and greater visibility can change the status of a language without necessarily eliminating the social attitudes that surround it.

vocabulary.zh: adv. 必然地, 必须地, 必要地
vocabulary.en:
r. in an essential manner
r. as a highly likely consequence
vocabulary.example: This suggests that official recognition and greater visibility can change the status of a language without necessarily eliminating the social attitudes that surround it.

vocabulary.zh: vt. 除去, 排除, 剔除, 消除
vocabulary.en:
v. kill in large numbers
v. remove from a contest or race
v. remove (an unknown variable) from two or more equations
vocabulary.example: This suggests that official recognition and greater visibility can change the status of a language without necessarily eliminating the social attitudes that surround it.

vocabulary.zh:
vt. 包围, 环绕, 围绕
n. 围绕物
vocabulary.en: v. extend on all sides of simultaneously; encircle
vocabulary.example: This suggests that official recognition and greater visibility can change the status of a language without necessarily eliminating the social attitudes that surround it.

vocabulary.zh:
n. 影响力, 权力, 势力
vt. 影响, 改变
vocabulary.en:
n. a power to affect persons or events especially power based on prestige etc
n. causing something without any direct or apparent effort
n. a cognitive factor that tends to have an effect on what you do
n. the effect of one thing (or person) on another
vocabulary.example: Attitudes towards a language can influence whether families continue to pass it from one generation to the next.

vocabulary.zh:
vt. 比...活得长, 生存, 生还, 幸免于
vi. 活下来, 幸存
vocabulary.en:
v. continue to live through hardship or adversity
v. continue in existence after (an adversity, etc.)
vocabulary.example: For minority languages, this is important because the process of parents passing a language on to their children is one of the main ways a language survives.

vocabulary.zh:
n. 同等的人, 匹敌, 贵族
vi. 凝视, 窥视, 费力地看, 隐现
vt. 与...同等, 封为贵族
vocabulary.en:
n. a person who is of equal standing with another in a group
n. a nobleman (duke or marquis or earl or viscount or baron) who is a member of the British peerage
v. look searchingly
vocabulary.example: They may also see Welsh-speaking adults and peers using the language outside the home.

vocabulary.zh:
a. 有用的, 良好的, 赞成的, 顺利的
[医] 良好的, 顺利的
vocabulary.en:
a encouraging or approving or pleasing
a (of winds or weather) tending to promote or facilitate
s occurring at a convenient or suitable time
s presaging or likely to bring good luck
vocabulary.example: Research with children in Wales has found that those educated through the medium of Welsh tend to have more favourable attitudes towards the language than their English-medium peers.

vocabulary.zh:
n. 暴露, 揭发, 揭露
[化] 曝光量; 照射; 照射量
vocabulary.en:
n. vulnerability to the elements; to the action of heat or cold or wind or rain; 
n. the act of subjecting someone to an influencing experience
n. the disclosure of something secret
n. aspect resulting from the direction a building or window faces
vocabulary.example: Exposure to Welsh-speaking people and communities can also help to build positive attitudes.

vocabulary.zh:
adv. 相对地, 比较地, 相当地, 相关地
[计] 相对地
vocabulary.en: r. in a relative manner; by comparison to something else
vocabulary.example: But there is still relatively little research into how Welsh speakers and non-Welsh speakers, perceive the language and its speakers.

vocabulary.zh: vt. 感觉, 认知, 理解, 意识到
vocabulary.en:
v. to become aware of through the senses
v. become conscious of
vocabulary.example: But there is still relatively little research into how Welsh speakers and non-Welsh speakers, perceive the language and its speakers.

vocabulary.zh:
a. 制度的, 公共机构的, 学会的
[法] 组织机构的, 制度的, 公共机构的
vocabulary.en:
a. relating to or constituting or involving an institution
a. organized as or forming an institution
vocabulary.example: Their children are growing up with greater opportunities to learn and use Welsh, and with more social and institutional support for doing so.

vocabulary.zh: adv. 自动地, 机械地
vocabulary.en: r. in a reflex manner
vocabulary.example: But Patsy’s experience in that Cardiff cafe shows that greater visibility and official support do not automatically make prejudice disappear.

vocabulary.zh: vi. 消失, 不见
vocabulary.en: v. get lost, as without warning or explanation
vocabulary.example: But Patsy’s experience in that Cardiff cafe shows that greater visibility and official support do not automatically make prejudice disappear.

vocabulary.zh: vi. 属于, 合适
vocabulary.en:
v. be owned by; be in the possession of
v. be suitable or acceptable
v. be in the right place or situation
v. be rightly classified in a class or category
vocabulary.example: The challenge for Welsh is therefore no longer simply to establish whether the language belongs in public life.

vocabulary.zh:
vt. 确定, 保证, 担保, 保护
[经] 确保, 确定
vocabulary.en:
v make certain of
v be careful or certain to do something; make certain of something
vocabulary.example: It is to ensure that people feel able to use it there without being made to feel rude, difficult or out of place.

cloze.title: 四选一完形填空
cloze.instruction: 阅读节选，为每一空选择最符合原文语境的选项，每题只有一个正确答案。

parts.text: That was the complaint a stranger directed at Patsy, a Welsh learner featured in my latest book, after

her family speaking Welsh in a Cardiff cafe. She could hardly believe it: “But you’re in Wales. What are you talking about?”

Wales has come a long way since the days of the Welsh not, a
token often accompanied by corporal punishment that was used in some 19th-century schools to discourage children from speaking Welsh. The Welsh

is now more visible, more widely supported and more politically protected than at any point in history.

But my ongoing research of Welsh-speaking families living in Cardiff suggests that while attitudes have improved
, some linguistic prejudice still lingers beneath the surface. The pattern is not unique to Wales. I found similar experiences among Finland’s Swedish-speaking

, where official recognition of the language has not always translated into acceptance in everyday life.

Several of the Welsh-speaking parents I interviewed had experienced
attitudes towards Welsh when they were growing up in the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s. One father remembered being verbally

for speaking Welsh in Cardiff as a child. Yet he was clear that things had changed.

Other participants described being stereotyped or made to feel uncomfortable because they spoke Welsh. They felt that such prejudice was less

today, but could still appear in subtle ways, sometimes disguised as humour.

One Welsh-speaking teacher described becoming more

of negative attitudes towards Welsh after moving from a Welsh-medium school to an English-medium one. The difference between generations was notable. Parents in my study could recall experiences of stereotyping,
or prejudice. Their children had experienced very little of this.

questions.evidence: But my ongoing research of Welsh-speaking families living in Cardiff suggests that while attitudes have improved dramatically, some linguistic prejudice still lingers beneath the surface.

questions.explanation: 原文此处使用 minority（minority）。结合上下文辨认词义与词形。
questions.evidence: I found similar experiences among Finland’s Swedish-speaking minority, where official recognition of the language has not always translated into acceptance in everyday life.

questions.evidence: Several of the Welsh-speaking parents I interviewed had experienced negative attitudes towards Welsh when they were growing up in the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s.

questions.explanation: 原文此处使用 abused（abuse）。结合上下文辨认词义与词形。
questions.evidence: One father remembered being verbally abused for speaking Welsh in Cardiff as a child.

questions.evidence: One Welsh-speaking teacher described becoming more aware of negative attitudes towards Welsh after moving from a Welsh-medium school to an English-medium one.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Minority language speakers continue to face prejudice in different European settings.
Better preparation for teachers is central to supporting pupils with dyslexia.
Private schooling can reinforce class separation and wider social divisions.
Schools can reduce some learning gaps while advantages linked to family wealth persist.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: But there is still relatively little research into how Welsh speakers and non-Welsh speakers, perceive the language and its speakers.

questions.prompt: What does the research suggest despite improving attitudes towards Welsh?
options: Language attitudes have no social consequences.
Every trace of prejudice has disappeared.
Welsh is no longer spoken by any family.
questions.explanation: 第 4 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: But my ongoing research of Welsh-speaking families living in Cardiff suggests that while attitudes have improved dramatically, some linguistic prejudice still lingers beneath the surface.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 10?
options: They felt that such prejudice was less obvious today, but could still appear in subtle ways, sometimes disguised as humour.
The experiences of the Welsh speakers became even more interesting when I compared them with those of Swedish speakers in Finland.
Younger participants had also grown up in an environment where Welsh was more visible and where there were more opportunities to use it outside the home.
The incidents happened in different countries and involved different languages but the pattern was similar.
questions.explanation: 定位第 10 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: The experiences of the Welsh speakers became even more interesting when I compared them with those of Swedish speakers in Finland.

“This suggests that official recognition and greater visibility can change the status of a language without necessarily eliminating the social attitudes that surround it.”
